'''Richart Elliott Slusher''' (born 1938) is a regents researcher and a principal research scientist at the [[Georgia Tech Research Institute]], and the director of the [[Georgia Tech Quantum Institute]].

==Early life and education==
Slusher was born in 1938. He received a Ph.D. in physics from the [[University of California at Berkeley]] in 1965.<ref name="about">{{cite web|url=http://www.gtqi.gatech.edu/peopleGTRI.shtml?personId=slusher|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805142143/http://www.gtqi.gatech.edu/peopleGTRI.shtml?personId=slusher|archive-date=2020-08-05|title=Richart E. Slusher|publisher=[[Georgia Tech Quantum Institute]]|accessdate=2011-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Physicist To Be Honored at ILS-XI |url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/199510/ils.cfm |access-date=2022-04-14 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Slusher worked at [[Bell Laboratories]] from 1965 to 2007, where he directed a research department focused on optical and quantum device physics from 1977 to 2005. Since 2005, he has worked at the [[Georgia Tech Research Institute]].<ref name="about"/>

==Awards==
Slusher received the 1989 [[Einstein Prize for Laser Science]], the 1995 [[Arthur L. Schawlow Prize in Laser Science]] from the [[American Physical Society]] and the 2006 [[Max Born Award]] from the [[Optical Society of America]].<ref name="about"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Slusher&first_nm=Richart&year=1995|title=1995 Arthur L. Schawlow Prize in Laser Science Recipient|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]|accessdate=2011-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.osa.org/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/maxborn/default.aspx|title=Max Born Award|publisher=[[Optical Society of America]]|accessdate=2011-05-08}}</ref>
